subject: general
question: Researchers from which institutions discovered a new prion called SNG2 in January 2025?

options.text: Delhi University and Council of Scientific & Industrial Research - Delhi
Amity University - Mohali and Institute of Microbial Technology - Chandigarh

solution:
The correct answer is __**Amity University - Mohali and Institute of Microbial Technology - Chandigarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **January 2025**, a team of researchers from **Amity University, Mohali** and the **Council of Scientific & Industrial Research - Institute of Microbial Technology (CSIR-IMTECH), Chandigarh**, announced the discovery of a novel prion.
 
• The newly identified prion has been named **SNG2**, an acronym for **Supersaturating Non-Amyloidogenic Globular 2**.
 
• This discovery is a landmark in the field of **molecular biology** as it identifies a prion that behaves differently from traditional disease-causing proteins.
 
• The **SNG2** prion was discovered in the yeast species **Saccharomyces cerevisiae**, which is a common model organism used for studying cellular processes.
 
• Unlike pathological prions that form toxic **amyloid fibrils**, **SNG2** forms **globular structures** that are **non-amyloidogenic**, meaning they do not aggregate into the stiff fibers typical of neurodegenerative diseases.
 
• The researchers found that **SNG2** acts as a functional switch, helping the organism survive and adapt under **environmental stress**, such as nutrient deprivation or temperature changes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Prions and Proteostasis:** 
 
 
• Prions are **misfolded proteins** that can induce normal versions of the same protein to also misfold. This chain reaction usually leads to **protein aggregation**.
 
• In humans, prions are notorious for causing fatal conditions like **Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD)** and **Kuru**, as well as **Mad Cow Disease** in cattle.
 
 
 
• **Functional Prions:**
 
 
• While many prions are harmful, "functional prions" are those that provide a biological benefit. **SNG2** is a prime example of a **functional prion** that assists in **cellular memory** and stress response.
 
• This discovery suggests that protein-based **epigenetic inheritance** is more diverse and common than previously understood.
 
 
 
• **The Role of SNG2:**
 
 
• The **SNG2** protein remains in a **supersaturated state** within the cell until triggered by stress.
 
• Its **non-amyloidogenic** nature is crucial because it allows the cell to utilize the protein's aggregated form without suffering the **cellular toxicity** that usually leads to cell death in amyloid-related diseases.
 
 
 
• **Institutions Involved:**
 
 
• **Amity University, Mohali** is a leading private research university in **Punjab**, known for its focus on **biotechnology**.
 
• **CSIR-IMTECH**, located in **Chandigarh**, is a premier national laboratory under the **Ministry of Science and Technology**, specializing in **microbial engineering** and protein science.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The discovery of **SNG2** in **2025** provides new insights into how proteins can store information and help organisms adapt to their surroundings without changing their **DNA**.
 
• The study utilized advanced **biophysical techniques** and **fluorescence microscopy** to observe the transition of the protein into its **globular prion state**.
 
• Understanding the mechanism of **non-amyloidogenic** prions like **SNG2** could eventually lead to new therapeutic strategies for human diseases like **Alzheimer’s** and **Parkinson’s**, by teaching scientists how to prevent proteins from forming toxic **amyloid** clumps.
 
• This research underscores the importance of **inter-institutional collaboration** in **India** for achieving breakthroughs in fundamental **biological sciences**.
